neighbours.label: ' which' opening a non-restrictive relative clause after a comma
fire: The bridge was closed for repairs last week, which caused long delays downtown.
She was offered the job in Denver, which she accepted without hesitation.
The team lost its third game in a row, which put the coach under pressure.
Prices rose sharply in the spring, which hurt small bakeries most.
He sold the old farmhouse to his cousin, which surprised the whole family.
The museum reopened after the renovation, which took almost two years.
Our flight was rerouted through Chicago, which added four hours to the trip.
The senator voted against the bill, which angered many of her supporters.
quiet: The bridge was closed for repairs last week, and this caused long delays downtown.
She was offered the job in Denver, and she accepted without hesitation.
The team lost its third game in a row, putting the coach under pressure.
Prices rose sharply in the spring, hurting small bakeries most.
He sold the old farmhouse to his cousin, who had always wanted it.
The museum reopened after the renovation, where crowds gathered at once.
Our flight was rerouted through Chicago, so the trip took four hours longer.
The senator voted against the bill; many of her supporters were angry.
